query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Preheat the build platform to 350–500 °C during L-PBF processing of cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder to reduce thermal gradients.
generation.material_initial_state: Cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock prepared by mechanical alloying.
generation.intervention: Maintain an elevated, controlled substrate (build plate) temperature within the range of 350–500 °C during the L-PBF process.
generation.conditions: Applicable during L-PBF processing at standard energy densities; requires precise temperature control and monitoring; tested within the stated thermal window.
generation.structural_mediator: More uniform and equiaxed microstructure with significantly reduced directional thermal gradients.
generation.mechanism: Preheating the build platform decreases the thermal differential between the melt pool and the substrate, reducing rapid cooling-induced thermal stresses. This facilitates enhanced elemental diffusion, minimizing segregation and defect nucleation while refining the microstructure.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant reduction in residual stress and segregation-induced defects, coupled with improved mechanical integrity, compared to parts manufactured on a room-temperature build plate.
generation.baseline: Conventional L-PBF processing with a room-temperature substrate.
generation.boundary: Valid for laser powder bed fusion processes with high thermal inputs; results depend on maintaining the preheat within 350–500 °C and may not apply to non-laser-based AM methods.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism is well-supported, the precise optimal temperature and magnitude of improvement depend on further empirical validation with in-situ temperature monitoring and stress measurements.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct an L-PBF study where identical specimens are built with a room-temperature substrate versus substrates preheated to temperatures in 350–500 °C. Use incremental steps (e.g., 350 °C, 400 °C, 450 °C, 500 °C) to identify the optimal range.
measurements: Microstructural characterization using SEM/EDS and EBSD for grain size and segregation analysis
Mechanical testing including tensile strength, hardness, and fracture toughness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If specimens produced with the preheated substrate do not exhibit statistically significant reductions in residual stress and segregation, or if mechanical properties fail to improve over the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Multi-component alloys containing Co, Cr, Ni and other elements have attracted attention recently []. Equiatomic CoCrNi MEAs in particular demonstrate high strength and ductility at low temperatures []. CoCrNi MEAs are typically manufactured by casting and powder metallurgy, yielding a room temperature yield strength of only 360 MPa. Higher mechanical properties require additional processing like rolling, heat treatment and high pressure torsion []. Mechanical alloying (MA) combined with spark plasma sintering (SPS) can also produce CoCrNi MEAs with improved mechanics []. Traditional casting has some shortcomings such as low solidification rate, element segregation and rough casting microstructure, which requires heat treatment to optimize the structure. Compared to traditional casting, LAM can fabricate complex geometries []. LAM enables high cooling rates and temperature gradients, yielding refined solid solution phases and microstructures well-suited for high quality CoCrNi MEAs. Research on CoCrNi MEAs with LAM remains limited. There are many articles on LAM of CoCrNi MEAs. but there are very few articles on HSLAM CoCrNi MEAs. Our objective is to contrast the SRO in these materials, thereby discerning the impacts of solidification quench rates and thermal treatment on SRO formation. Moreover, we have selected CoCrNi, CoCrFeNi, and CoCrFeMnNi for comparative analysis, potentially revealing insights into how compositional complexity influences SRO formation. High entropy alloys (HEAs) and their closely related variants, called multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), are the topic of a rather new area of research, and so far, the gathered knowledge is incomplete. This is especially true when it comes to material libraries, as the fabrication of HEA and MPEA samples with a wide variation in chemical compositions is challenging in itself. Additive manufacturing technologies are, to date, seen as possibly the best option to quickly fabricate HEA and MPEA samples, offering both the melting metallurgical and solid-state sintering approach. Within this study, CrFeNiTi MPEA samples were fabricated via laser powder-bed fusion (PBF-LB) and solid-state sintering of mechanically alloyed powder feedstock. The main emphasis is on the PBF-LB process, while solid-state sintering serves as benchmark. Within a volumetric energy density (VED) window of 50 J/mm3 to 83 J/mm3, dense samples with large defect-free sections and an average micro-hardness of 965 HV0.1 were fabricated. Clear correlations between the local chemical alloy composition and the related micro-hardness were recorded, with the main factor being the evaporation of titanium at higher VED
